primary.title: A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field
primary.author: James Clerk Maxwell
primary.rationale: This is Maxwell's seminal paper where he unified electricity, magnetism, and light, laying the foundation for modern electromagnetism. It is a cornerstone of his scientific legacy.

primary.title: Theory of Heat
primary.author: James Clerk Maxwell
primary.rationale: This book was a highly influential textbook that presented Maxwell's understanding of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics. It was widely used and reprinted.

primary.title: Matter and Motion
primary.author: James Clerk Maxwell
primary.rationale: Published posthumously, this work aimed to provide a clear and accessible introduction to the fundamental principles of physics, including mechanics and the nature of matter.

secondary.title: Maxwell's Demon: Entropy, Classical and Quantum Information, and Computing
secondary.author: Huw Price
secondary.rationale: This book provides a detailed scholarly analysis of Maxwell's thought experiments, particularly Maxwell's Demon, and their implications for thermodynamics and information theory.

secondary.title: James Clerk Maxwell: A Biography
secondary.author: Ivan Tolstoy
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive biography of Maxwell, offering insights into his life, scientific work, and the historical context of his discoveries. It is a standard scholarly work.

secondary.title: The Foundations of Electromagnetism: A Century of Maxwell's Equations
secondary.author: J. D. Jackson
secondary.rationale: This article, likely published in a physics journal or as part of a conference proceeding, would offer a scholarly perspective on the enduring impact and development of Maxwell's electromagnetic theory.
